CreateTopic.summary: A topic is the smallest unit for subscription and publishing in DataHub. You can use a topic to represent a category or type of stream data.

schema.description:
Topic type. Currently, Tuple and BLOB types are supported:  

1. A BLOB-type topic supports writing a block of binary data as a single record.  
2. A Tuple-type topic supports records similar to those in a database. Each record contains multiple columns and requires a RecordSchema. Because data is transmitted over the network as strings, the schema is needed to transform the data into the appropriate types.

Topic expansion mode. After this mode is enabled, shards support horizontal scaling and no longer support merging or splitting. The number of shards can only increase and cannot decrease. Once enabled, you can consume the topic using Kafka-compatible methods.

Enables multi-version schema support. After this feature is enabled, a topic can have multiple schemas simultaneously. You can choose one schema to write data, and the consumer automatically parses each record based on the version marked in the data (parsing fails if the schema corresponding to the version has been deleted).  

> Enabling multi-version schema has the following impacts:  
1. You can no longer use the appendFields API.  
2. You can perform create, read, update, and delete operations on schemas.  
3. Connectors are created using the latest version of the schema.
